result.title: Learning Whom to Trust About the Unseen: Source Credibility and Reliability Transfer in Language Models
result.summary: A source who has been right before deserves attention, but about what? We ask how far a demonstrated record of reliability travels in language models when the new claim cannot be checked, and whether the answer depends on the kind of claim. Three behavioral studies across six models approach the question from three angles. Study 1 adapts the Einstein-effect paradigm and finds that models, unlike the human sample, favor a spiritual leader over a scientist for the same obscure statement, and that the preference largely reverses when the statement is reworded in the vocabulary of physics. Study 2 adapts a paradigm in which a trusted expert calls a scientific or religious explanation unknown or a mystery; models reproduce the human domain asymmetry in exaggerated form. Study 3, the central test, gives two fictional informants different records on checkable river forecasts and then has them endorse matched claims about hidden natural and spiritual causes of the same village events. Most models carry the record to natural causes and barely at all to spiritual ones; one model transfers it weakly to either. Telling the model that the reliable informant forecasts by spiritual guidance rather than by measurement lowers that informant's influence on natural claims in every model and produces no comparable gain on spiritual claims in any. Demonstrated reliability thus has a scope in these models, and the account a source gives of how they came to be reliable can narrow it. Whether this reflects a judgment about relevance or the low prior credence of spiritual claims is the question the design leaves open, and we outline the experiment that would settle it.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用三项行为实验考察六个语言模型能否把信息源已证实的可靠性迁移到无法核验的新主张上，发现迁移存在领域边界：可靠性主要作用于自然类主张，几乎不迁移到灵性类主张，且源对自身可靠性来源的解释会进一步收窄其影响范围。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽无视觉模态与 latent 状态，但其「可靠性作用范围随主张类型与来源解释而变」的发现，可为 LVR 中视觉证据与文本线索的加权、证据筛选提供概念性参照，是否涉及模型的内部证据使用尚待核查。
